notes:
CRM notes:
- Background: Proxima builds inference stack for autonomous fleet control and operator tools. Very latency sensitive for control-plane prompts (~p95 < 100ms target).
- Use case specifics: real-time-control (short prompts, single-token decode often), telemetry-summarization (longer outputs 150-800 tokens), and reranking for sensor fusion (~multiple candidate scoring).
- Observed baseline from infra team (sample week): steady-state ~150 QPS average, avg tokens per request ~256 -> ~38.4k tokens/sec steady; bursts observed during fleet sync up to 1,200 QPS for 60-120s -> ~307k tokens/sec. Traffic pattern: predictable daily peaks + occasional global sync bursts.
- Customer asked for throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) and latency SLOs. Wants reserved capacity plan that covers steady-state + 40% headroom, with burst capacity handled by autoscale/burst pool.
- Proposed Redwood sizing (initial): reserved pool equivalent to 12x H100 for steady-state headroom (est to meet 40k-50k tokens/sec with p95 <120ms) + 4x H100 burst nodes for handling short-term peaks with autoscale. Will test quantized 4-bit runtimes and KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost; expected 1.8-2.5x effective throughput gain from batching + caching.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 100-120ms, p99 <= 300-350ms for control prompts. Must include SLA credit language tied to p95/p99 buckets.
- SLA negotiation points: uptime 99.95% target, latency SLOs with financial credits, guaranteed capacity lead time (30-45 days), model fallback policies (Redwood-hosted fallback if private pool saturated), data residency & KMS integration, breach response and on-call escalation window (30 min).
- Network / infra asks: 100Gbps node NICs, private VPC peering, egress caps called out. Also asked for sample rack / power footprint for on-prem install (per their data center constraints).
- Cost sensitivity: procurement favors capEX OPP for on-prem purchase but wants OPEX option for burst billing. Finance request: 3-year TCO comparison (Redwood Dedicated reserved + burst vs pure on-prem).
- Quote from CTO on call: "We need determinism more than cheapest unit price — predictable tail latency is what matters for safety cases."
- Open questions: fine-grained token accounting for metrics/chargeback, expected ML infra team runbook for model upgrades, legal for data residency clause.
- Next steps (short): run 2-day detailed sizing workshop (still on calendar 2025-11-18/19), Redwood to run bench matrix (model variants, quantization levels, batching configs) and deliver bench report. SE (Diego) to prepare reference config templates and cost scenarios.
